name: [Platform] 16 Failure Handler

parameters.content:
## Dead-letter log

n8n fires an error workflow for **production** executions only, never for a
manual test run. A failure here therefore means a real webhook or scheduled run
broke, which is exactly the set worth alerting on.

The Error Trigger does not hand over the failing run’s input, so the trace id
and tenant are recovered from the error payload when they appear in it and left
blank when they do not. The execution URL is always recorded, and it is always
enough for a human to read the original input.

## Replay

A replay re-submits a lead through 14 with `force: true`, because without it the
lead ledger would suppress the re-run as a duplicate and the replay would
silently do nothing.

`dry_run` still defaults to true. A replay is not a licence to write.

The failure table is append-only: a replay adds a row referencing the original
`failure_id` rather than overwriting it, so the history of what broke and what
was done about it stays intact.

## Replay suite

Three fixtures covering the replay leg: a valid replay that reaches 14, one with
no lead, and one with a malformed tenant.

The Error Trigger leg above is deliberately not covered here. n8n fires an error
workflow for production executions only, so exercising it from a test would mean
deliberately breaking a live run. It is verified by the fact that a failure
appears in `swarm_failures` when one actually happens.

description: Dead-letter log for the revenue pipeline. Captures any production failure in 11-15 with its trace id, failing node and execution URL, and offers an audited replay path that re-submits a lead through 14 with force set.
